question:
A 18-year-old female patient visits her PCP reporting chronic diarrhea characterized by malodorous,
loose stools and significant weight loss (35 pounds) over three years. She mentions a recent episode
of a pruritic, papular rash on her elbows and forearms that spontaneously resolved after two months.
She has no history of camping or international travel. Clinical examination reveals a thin patient with
pallor of the conjunctiva and skin, and mild abdominal distention. Which diagnostic test would be most
appropriate to confirm the suspected diagnosis? Answer Choices: (A) Fecal fat quantification (B)
Serum IgA level assessment (C) Stool test for ova and parasites (D) Stool ova and parasite
examination (E) Serum anti-endomysial antibody assay (F) Upper gastrointestinal barium study (G)
Small bowel endoscopy and biopsy (H) Colonoscopy with biopsy (I) Serum anti-tissue
transglutaminase antibody assay (J) Serum anti-gliadin antibody test
 A. Colonoscopy with biopsy
B. Serum IgA level assessment
C. Small bowel endoscopy and biopsy
D. Upper gastrointestinal barium study
E. Serum anti-gliadin antibody test
F. Stool test for ova and parasites
G. Stool ova and parasite examination
H. Serum anti-tissue transglutaminase antibody assay
I. Serum anti-endomysial antibody assay
J. Fecal fat quantification
